T.S. Shure Numbers Wooden Magnets 20 Piece MagnaFun Set [[VIDEOID:e0d01cc825ab0e8a78139d698bca33d5]] When I first saw how thin the magnets on these pieces were, I thought that they wouldn't stick at all. But, they ended up sticking pretty well. I guess you don't want them to stick so well that a 3-year-old can't pull them off. In my video, I show how they stick to a piece of metal, and they also stuck to my fridge, and all other metallic surfaces.

The construction of the pieces was good. The box was just okay. I had a hard time pealing all of the stickers off the box, which I needed to do to open the box. Also, once I took all of the magnets out, it took a long time to cram them back in so that the box would re-close. Forget having a toddler do this on their own, but if you lose about four pieces, then you should be able to easily fit the remaining pieces. But, I'd recommend throwing the box away, and finding your own box.

They have the numbers 1-20, with the corresponding number of things on the piece. For example, piece number 17 has seventeen butterflies.

Pros:
+Really sticks to a fridge or other surface
+Has the numbers 1-20, with a corresponding illustration
+Teaches new words like clownfish, cardinal, construction worker, flamingo
+The pieces are good quality

Cons:
-The pictures with larger numbers have too many things that are too small for a young child to easily count
-In order for a toddler to clean these up, you'll need to find a replacement box
-The magnets aren't super strong
text_fidelity_b: T.S. Shure Numbers Wooden Magnets 20 Piece MagnaFun Set

text_fidelity_a:
QOGELY Home Decor Blaster Building Kits This is not a “puzzle”, but a “model”. I can only assume that they do not have a word for “model” in Chinese. Because Chinese companies always list items like this is a “puzzle” though it’s really not.

This model is made of wood. It shows to have 47 pieces. There are 3 boards with the cutout pieces. You’ll want to use caution when removing the pieces from the boards so that you do not break them. You remove the pieces from the boards as you go. The pieces are numbered on the instruction sheet, but not on the boards. So if you remove them all at 1st, it will make it very difficult to put the model together. I highly recommend you have either a razor blade or thin sharp knife available to help remove the pieces. If you simply use your fingers, you could easily break a piece.

I must admit that I am not a person who likes to build models. So it took me about an hour and ½ to put this together. It turned out okay, but not as perfect as the pictures. The shingles do not fit perfectly. Nonetheless I think it looks okay.

Also, when you get to pieces 12, 13, 14 and 15 which is part of instruction number 5… Those 4 pieces make a little platform. The way the instruction show it on instruction number 9, that platform sits inside section B. But if you place it there, then the top shingle portion sits on top of the platform and is not sturdy. If you don’t put that platform there, then the top piece see fits in to the bottom piece a which makes it sturdy. Then I use that platform as a base on the bottom to place the temple on top of. Written on that platform is “Temple of Serenity”. So because of that, I think it should go on the bottom is a base anyway. But of course you can do it anyway you want to.

An optional string of LED lights is included. Two AA batteries are required and not included.

As a bonus, there is also a small “Ellie House” which is 24 pieces.

This model is made in China and being sold by a Chinese company on Amazon. At the current price of 30 bucks I think it is a bit expensive, but it is a unique and interesting item. Also, it comes in a nice cardboard box, which makes it easy for wrapping if you’re giving it as a gift.
text_fidelity_b: QOGELY Home Decor Blaster Building Kits

Ludonaute Fantasy Flight Games LUCV01 Carta Imperia Victoria, Multicolor CIV is a very good small card game. It takes about a half hour to play, and is largely comprised of cards with silly cartoonish art on them representing science, military, culture and so forth. Basically, if it's in Sid Meier's Civilization, it has been boiled down and reduced to a small concept here.

The artwork is...interesting. Some people will love it's uniqueness, while others will find it to be off-putting. I tend to fall in the latter column - it doesn't look like it matches with the theme of the game at all. The player aids are good, but small (probably to fit in the box), and can be difficult to read. It would have been better, in my opinion, to put some more text on each individual card instead of trying to stuff all the text onto one very small aid.

text_fidelity_a: Little Tikes Cozy Truck Ride-On with removable floorboard I only give two stars rather than one because it looks cool. Putting this thing together is a royal pita. First of all you better have some tools because parts do NOT fit correctly. The left front wheel assembly slides up from the bottom and is attached with a pressed on fastener which was no problem for the right side however the left side did not have any metal sticking up past the bushing. I had to take a Dremel tool and cut the pinched metal that stops the washer so that I could get enough of the rod to attach a fastener. The steering wheel is locked in place with a clip that is inserted into the plastic rod that goes into the dash and is supposed to go through a plastic ring that you place on the rod from the other side of the dash. Well I pushed as hard as I could and there is no way this was going to connect. If it would have connected there is no way a child would be able to turn the steering wheel. I had to elongate the holes in the steering column in order to get this connected. Bottom line is this product is severely lacking in quality control. I would not buy another one because of this problem By the way, I'm not someone who usually has trouble putting things together and I have quite a large collection of tools that I know how to use otherwise I don't see anyway this thing gets put together.

Thames & Kosmos Wind Power V4.0 STEM Experiment Kit | Build a 3ft Wind Turbine to Generate Electricity | Learn About Renewable Energy & Power a Small Model Car | Weatherproof for Outdoor Use This kit was a lot more fun for Dad than it was for the kid. She's younger than the recommended age range, but had little trouble putting the whole model together in under 30 minutes with Dad's help. We barely used the book for assembly, but read the more educational "science" book cover to cover.

She and I talk all the time about renewable energy, largely because solar panels are looking like the next big home improvement project around here, and we get what I'd consider a reasonable amount of wind. She found the concepts easy enough to understand, and was interested to see what we'd be able to do in the backyard...and it's not much. The wind we got was not nearly enough to make this project effective, even on what I'd consider a relatively windy day. I put it on the roof for a short time and that helped, but not much. The turbine requires a battery, which makes both of us question where the small amount of power we are generating actually comes from.

So the experiments died off rather quickly, and this became a very short model building project for her that Dad is enjoying tinkering with to see if he can charge one of those rechargable cell-phone batteries. Kid is off playing with the very small toy car that comes with the kit, but doesn't look like it belongs at all.

If you get a lot of wind, then it's probably a lot more fun, but it's for the younger age of the spectrum for sure.
text_fidelity_b: Thames & Kosmos Wind Power V4.0 STEM Experiment Kit | Build a 3ft Wind Turbine to Generate Electricity | Learn About Renewable Energy & Power a Small Model Car | Weatherproof for Outdoor Use

Colorforms 70th Anniversary Set - The Classic Picture Toy That Sticks Like Magic - Ages 3+ I'm in my 60's and remember Colorforms from when I was a kid. It was and still is in my opinion one of the greatest toys around. Shapes are placed onto a background board and they cling to the board, so the possibilities of creating designs and story scenes are endless.

I do a lot of geometric designing so have a reproduction of the original set, and this anniversary set makes a great addition. The original set is all basic single color shapes. These anniversary sheets (consisting of 4 separate unbound sheets) have those same shapes plus more, and some of these have multiple colors in one shape, with some of those colors being in different patterns and shades as opposed to being all solid colors. There ARE some solid colors, but there are also patterns with stripes, dots, triangles, circles inside of circles, half moons, etc. So this set expands on the designing possibilities with the added dimensions of patterns and color shades. As with the original set, these shapes are peeled off the page they come on and are then placed onto a black background sheet (included) which they cling to until removed.

These sheets are smaller than the original set that comes in a plastic spiral bound book. So if you already have the original in its box, you can just take these sheets from this anniversary set and store in with the original if you don't want to store 2 separate boxes. Overall a nice set that is great as an artsy and learning tool for kids and designing tool for adults who enjoy working with geometric shapes.
text_fidelity_b: Colorforms 70th Anniversary Set - The Classic Picture Toy That Sticks Like Magic - Ages 3+

text_fidelity_a:
PlayMonster Break in™ Alcatraz Make sure you know what you are getting yourself into before purchasing this item. I think it is a great item for the right person/people. If you are the type of person who likes participating in an escape room, or think you might like to participate in an escape room, then this might be for you. But this is not a game of chance. There is no luck. You do not roll the dice, or pick a card. You must complete each task before continuing. You either get the task right, or wrong. If you get it wrong, then there are hints to help, if you choose to use them.

It takes about 2 hours to complete. It could take you more time if you don’t use the hints, and perhaps less time if you do use the hints. It’s played with between one and 6 players. Honestly, I think 6 players would be too many. If you had 6, I think four would be playing the game and two would be making sure the drinks and snacks keep flowing. ;-)

Once you complete this game, you will not play it again, because you already know how to complete all of the tasks. But you certainly could give it to friends who have not played it. Or, perhaps you could invite other friends over who had not played it before and you could assist them with it.

Once you remove the lid, you will find the different pieces. But do NOT open the box that is inside until you are given instructions to do so. There are tasks which must be completed before you open the box that is inside.

If you want to have an idea of how to get started, then I highly recommend that you do an online search for “Unfiltered Gamer Break In Alcatraz”. These are a couple of guys who will walk you through about the first 20 minutes. If you don’t want to go that far then you can simply watch until they have completed the 1st task so you know exactly what you need to do. Yes, this can be a little complicated, but if you at least watch them complete the 1st task, you’ll know how to get started.
text_fidelity_b: PlayMonster Break in™ Alcatraz

text_fidelity_a: BARWA 41 Pack Doll Clothes and Accessories 5 PCS Fashion Dresses 5 Tops 5 Pants Outfits 10 PCS Mini Dresses 10shoes 6 Necklace 5 Glasses for 11.5 inch Doll In fact, I just ordered another set. As an adult fashion doll collector and semi-professional photographer, I appreciate the fact that the clothes are from a variety of dolls. Some of the clothes are standard, wide hip Barbie size, while others are slimmer in the hips and torso (more like Model Muse) and still more fit dolls who are short and petite (like Barbie's sisters Skipper and Stacey). The Skipper and Stacey size tops look cute as midriff baring tops on a regular Barbie. I read a complaint below about the pants not fitting, but that's the way Mattel has been making pants since about 1999 when they introduced the first wide hip Barbie doll (the doll that we know today as a regular Barbie). The jeans are meant to fit below the waist and you have to tug to get them on and close them completely because they are meant to fit snugly. It's true, the clothing seams aren't always perfectly straight, but I have the same issue with Mattel Barbie clothes that I buy in person. Plus, the fabrics for these fashions are - for the most part - nicer than what Mattel has been offering lately. At the end of the day, when you consider that SINGLE ITEM Barbie brand clothing packs currently sell for $2.44 - $5.00 each, and Barbie brand complete fashion sets with shoes retail for $5.00 - $35.00 each, spending just under $2.00 for complete outfit is a great deal.

text_fidelity_a:
PLANET BAKE Donut Baking Kit - Vegan Chocolate Donuts with Pre-Measured Ingredients and No Added Sugar- Complete Chef Kit Idea for Boys and Girls ages 4-12 I'm not at all pleased with this donut kit. I like the idea -- a kit that includes everything needed to make baked, frosted donuts that kids (with supervision) can take on as a fun project. Unfortunately, the execution of the idea was not done well.

The items come in a flimsy cardboard box that is easily dented up in transit. It makes for a poor presentation should this be a gift item sent to child. Inside the box is a set of cheap silicone molds for the donuts, a packet of sprinkles and a sealed packet with the mixes. The sprinkle packet opened up in transit so there were sprinkles everywhere. Inside the sealed packet the frosting mix is in a pouch, but the donut mix is just loose in the pouch. Getting the frosting packet out was a very messy proposition.

Making the mix is simple (needs water and oil). The included silicone molds are very thin and flimsy, and need to be inserted into a muffin pan to minimize the chance of spilling. This is the step kids will need the most assistance with.

But even if the donuts bake properly, they are no treat to eat. The chocolate flavor is not pleasant, and is made even worse by the artificial sweetener aftertaste. The texture is not bad considering these are gluten-free, but the taste is not good to the point where these are barely (and I mean barely!) edible.

Two stars for the overall concept of a donut kit as a fun kid project (both making and decorating) but everything else is a fail.
text_fidelity_b: PLANET BAKE Donut Baking Kit - Vegan Chocolate Donuts with Pre-Measured Ingredients and No Added Sugar- Complete Chef Kit Idea for Boys and Girls ages 4-12

text_fidelity_a: Faber-Castell Do-Art Dot a Design Animals For ages 6 and up. The set comes with 6 "design sheets" for kids to paint, but there are only 3 designs (koala, turtle, or dolphin). You get one sheet with only black-and-white lines for an older child to paint and dot. You also get that same design with the main colors pre-printed and you only need to add dots of paint to the white dots in the design. The kit also comes with: 8 acrylic paints (light blue, dark blue, green, yellow-green, yellow, orange, red, purple), 2 fine tip dotters, 1 medium tip dotter, 1 brush, sticky tac (keeps paper flat while painting), 2 cardboard frames with hangers, and instructions. Acrylic paints can dry out quickly, so you may need to add water to the paints to keep them from drying out. Acrylic paints can quickly dry onto clothing and not come out, so you'll want to wear a painting smock. Wash dotters, brush (and work surface) before the paint dries if you intend to reuse them. The "dotters" are foam rounds on the end of a handle, and they create somewhat raised paint dots on the design sheets. It's a fun idea with colorful paints, but it is kind of simple so probably for younger kids rather than teenagers or older.

Magformers Magnets in Motion Set - Engineering Magnet Toys for Brain Development - 300 Pc Set I have bought three sets of magformers now for all of my grandchildren (3 to 14). Even toddlers can play with them because they are too large to swallow. They also like the solid shapes and colors of Magnatiles but those are more expensive. You can also get magnetic wooden blocks (Tegu) but those are really expensive so I haven't bought any.

The magformers are one of those toys that both kids and adults can sit and play with for an hour or longer. What I've noticed with three young grandkids together is that they each have their favorite pieces and styles of construction. One always creates vehicles, one creates houses, and the third makes towers. The colors and feel of the pieces are both soothing and exciting to work with.

Update: I had five kids and two adults playing with these recently and the person that seemed the most focused on building things is an MIT Neuroscientist. Once he built things following the guide, the kids quickly caught on and followed suit. I recommend that an adult work with the kids to begin with.

Regarding complaints about the magnets not working, if you snap together two piles of similarly shaped objects and then try to put the two piles together, sometimes the piles will reject each other. If you take one pile and start adding it to the other one at a time, all the pieces hold to each other. It seems as though the magnets must change polarity inside the plastic. I'd love a proper explanation.

I only recommend getting sets of 40 or more to have enough pieces to be creative. Wait for them to go on sale unless money is no object. Since all the grandkids took their sets home with them, I've bought a fourth set to keep at my house.

Addendum per request: I first chose these toys because of the brightly colored plastic material but soon discovered that having the pieces snap together and hold their shape is quite satisfying. While they don't take away from the joy of plain wooden blocks, they are different and allow you to vary how you play with them.

This particular kit is right for me because I'll have a crowd of five young children and many adults (thankfully two engineers) for two weeks over Christmas and I'll put this out on a large sofa table in the living room near the tree. That way the kids will feel like they have toys and waiting won't be so hard. It also incorporates many of the other kits you can buy separately so the kids can see specific types of builds.

Go to youtube and type in magformers to see how they are used. Construction is really that easy.
text_fidelity_b: Magformers Magnets in Motion Set - Engineering Magnet Toys for Brain Development - 300 Pc Set

Oltree | Cooperative Strategy Game for Teens and Adults | Ages 8+ | 2 to 4 Players | 60 Minutes Oltree is a cooperative board game based off of a French role playing game of the same name. I haven't heard of that game, but it's vaguely King Arthur-themed, and reeks of middle age knights and peasants stuff, minus the dragons.

I get the feeling that these are well-known characters in that universe, and I think that if you know who they are, that might add an extra layer of fun to the game. As it is, this game is very...dull. It has a story, and that story is quite predictable, and you'll end up replaying the same ten scenarios over again if you complete the campaign. The writing wasn't exactly bad, but nothing really stood out amongst any of the cards. The actions are largely mechanical, but it is fun the first few times you work to add a barracks to your castle or help a damsel in distress.

I will say that the best element of the game is the production value. This is the only version of this game (that I know of) and it feels like what you'd get from a $100+ Kickstarter campaign, with wooden everything and quality cards.

I think if the characters provided a bit more personality to the story, or if I knew something more about the world, I might really like this game, but I found it rather mechanical and slow moving, and the campaign didn't hook me as well as I'd hoped. It's not a bad game, but it wasn't for me.

text_fidelity_a:
Melissa & Doug Anteater Antics Action Game With 2 Plush Hats This is seriously one of the cutest games ever! I love the variety within it, too.

First of all, the anteaters themselves are very well made! You get two of them. Sometimes you get "masks" and they're pretty crappy, but these are quality. To wear these, there's two felt-like straps that will fit along the back of a child's head, along with velcro piece at the end of one strap. This means it will fit pretty much any child's head, because you can tighten or loosen as much of the strap as you want. There's another piece of velcro attached to the underside of the anteater's snout. This is what picks up the felt-like ants. Super, super cute!

Within this set is also the instructions, of course, along with a timer and a set of cards. These cards are similar to the cards within most matching games out there. We have several of them. They are small, square, and thick. One side of each of them simply shows an anteater at a picnic. The other side either shows various types of food for a matching game(This is also great for speech development!), or one or the other side of a colorful ant. This is also for matching, and a great way for the youngest players to learn colors. There are also a few "tummy ache" cards, which shows a sick anteater. A player will lose cards they've matched when this card comes into play.

You can really mix and match the various games in any way you want, especially depending on the ages involved. You can simply play "hide and seek" with the ants, or allow a player to find an ant once they find a match within the cards, or find the color of the ant they've matched together. You can add the timer for the older players or just to add a bit more challenge, if desired. You can also simply play a matching game with the cards for a quieter game. There are many possibilities for playing this game, so I imagine it will take longer to get "old" for most little ones.

Overall, this is a wonderful game, and one of the most fun ones we've had the pleasure of playing!
text_fidelity_b: Melissa & Doug Anteater Antics Action Game With 2 Plush Hats

Advantus 12 Inch Desktop World Globe with Blue Oceans (30502),13 W x 12 D x 15 H in Does a perfect globe exist? Probably it does, but I couldn’t afford it. I’m happy with this one although it isn’t perfect.
The good stuff: it came in a super sturdy box that held the globe stable during transport. (The manufacturer ships it, not Amazon.) The stand seems strong and sturdy, and of course I’m grateful for the 720° rotation. The colors are attractive. I even like the raised texture where there are mountain ranges. I’m glad that the United States is divided into states. Finally, although I’m not 100% educated on geography, I can say this globe is up-to-date enough for my purposes; for example, Sudan is divided into Sudan and South Sudan.
The less-good stuff: I’m surprised to see that Canada’s provinces are named, but not outlined! Unless the lines are just so fine that I can’t see them, you have to guess their boundaries. Some cities are identified in the US states, but I was really surprised to see that state capitals are not identified! I suppose some state capitals are named, but Austin Texas (where we live), Tallahassee Florida, and other states I’m familiar with have various cities but not their capitals identified! I also think that city placement is close, but not 100% accurate. Nevertheless, this globe will get a lot of use in homeschooling, and will serve our purposes. I would buy the same globe again if I needed to for some reason.
text_fidelity_b: Advantus 12 Inch Desktop World Globe with Blue Oceans (30502),13 W x 12 D x 15 H in

Discover with Dr. Cool PRO Series Rock Tumbler - Turn Rocks into Stunning Gemstones! At first I put this in the kitchen, I quickly learned that it was too loud for an open floor plan, it made me listen to tv on too high of a volume, so when I switched to the 2nd grit I moved it to a spare bedroom. This worked out great since I go in that room almost daily I was able to keep up with knowing when to change out to the next grit.

This is super easy to set up and get started. It comes with absolutely everything needed to go from start to finish including jewelry items to use so you can show off your stones. The instructions are very easy to follow along too.It also comes with activity books and the jewelry pieces are a necklace, a ring, a keychain and ear rings.

The instructions gives you an idea of how long the stones should tumble in each grit and at what speed.
This is what I did..
-grit #1..I did for 3 days on #3 speed
-grit#2.. I started at 5 days on #2…then opened it up and decided it needed a few more days since they were a bit rough so I did 2
more days on #3 setting
-grit#3.. I did for 7 days on #1 setting.
-grit#4..I did 7 days on #1. The smaller stones were great , the larger stones had a few blemishes yet, but I like things when they
aren’t perfect so they were great for me…I will be making them into necklaces once I put holes in them.

As you can see from my pictures from start to finish how much the rocks changed. Then at the end I wiped them off with mineral oil as suggested in the instructions. This has been an amazing experience to watch the rough rocks transform into smooth beautiful stones.
text_fidelity_b: Discover with Dr. Cool PRO Series Rock Tumbler - Turn Rocks into Stunning Gemstones!

Hasbro Elefun Snackin Safari Hasbro's new Elefun's Snackin Safari Game for children 3 and up has a wonderful concept for fun, if your child has a lot of patience. The game is made for 1 or 2 players. There are two elephant heads with handles connected to a long slinky trunk with a suction cup on the end. Included are 2 home base cards and 13 snack cards. The object of the game is to pick up a snack card with the suction cup, and there are 3 different ways to play the game.

The first way to play is to find the Golden Tutti Fruit Cake and be the winner. The second way is to collect all your matching colors to win and the third way is to get the most pairs of matching snacks to win. It sounds easy enough, until you realize that it takes a lot of patience to bounce the elephant's slinky trunk quickly and hard enough to actually suction a card to it. It could take 6 times or 60 times, as the slinky is a weak plastic one and the small suction cup needs to be pushed on a card to pick it up.

Surprisingly enough, the little ones loved the concept, but after a dozen tries to pick up a card, became frustrated. If Hasbro can tweak this game to make a stronger slinky and stronger suction cup, so the little ones can pick up a card after a few tries, this game would be a big hit. I hope Hasbro reads these reviews and makes this cute game less frustrating, as the kids will really enjoy it!
text_fidelity_b: Hasbro Elefun Snackin Safari

ThinkFun and Crazy Aaron's Thinking Putty Puzzle and STEM Toy for Boys and Girls Ages 8 and Up - The Famous Thinking Putty in Logic Game Form I’ve played many of Thinkfun’s logic puzzles, and use them in my classroom. So, I was very interested in their new logic puzzle that uses Crazy Aaron’s Putty. This game has some similarities with their other logic puzzles. It comes with 60 cards that show the challenge setup on one side and a possible answer on the back. The setup for each challenge takes the longest than any other logic puzzle because you have to tear the balls of putty off each color. It is challenging, even the first few challenges’ solutions aren’t immediately visible, they take some thought to solve.

I enjoyed this for myself and found it relaxing to put together and solve. I could see some kids not having the patience to play through the puzzle. I don’t plan to use this one in my classroom because I think the putty would get funky after having some kids play with it, and there could be some putty mixing that intentionally or unintentionally could happen and ruin the game.

Overall, this is a very clever idea. I’ve played the beginning challenges and enjoyed figuring them out. Kids will love the putty, but I’m not sure how long the challenges will hold their attention.

text_fidelity_a:
Arizona GameCo Smack it! Card Game for Kids | Ages 6-12 | Fun, Fast-paced and Easy to Learn | Family Game Night Friendly | a Great Boy or Girl Gift Idea Fairly fun game but card quality is poor for the price. I doubt this is a game to play for hours on end yet.....at the price point I would appreciate brand playing card quality. Is the game bad? I have "dealt" with worse.....there are certainly other card games....even Uno; cheaper, with better card quality but after all....this is a fast slap game. The cards feel cheap, look cheap and shuffle the same. They shuffle in a manegable way but to me this is almost disposable card stock quality. The "art" is non existent with numbers simple written and spelled on the card...colors also do not matter.
Your kids might just toss them on the table and mish mosh them to shuffle them. That will work fine. Slamwich has the excellent card quality and is also a fast easy slap game along this price point. If I had a re-do, I would just stick with Slamwich. Card stock is higher quality and game itself is a little more in depth and kids and adults enjoy a few rounds.

I cannot in good conscience recommend this at 8 dollars or higher. The gameplay itself is simple old fashioned war with a light/slight twist. Number cards....say a 14 verus a 32 dont matter at all (the 32 doesnt take the pile)....it is all about the "slap cards" and "challenege cards"...challenge is where your higher number card played actually counts for once. I DO see that very young kids would enjoy it. I do not see this being a "drinking game" or fun for adults without some extra house rules. Quality is simply subpar for the price. The business is in the USA, the cards and actual game itself are outsourced to China if that matters to you.

Rating is ....average. These are close or are average card size....they have a slick coat. The plain white background quickly picks up color bleed or whatever.....

It is not horrible but just eeks in at "ok" for simple card games. It isnt great and it isnt a big go to except for maybe the 7 year old children set...and the box states...6 plus for age and 2 to 7 people. I say...skip don't smack.
text_fidelity_b: Arizona GameCo Smack it! Card Game for Kids | Ages 6-12 | Fun, Fast-paced and Easy to Learn | Family Game Night Friendly | a Great Boy or Girl Gift Idea
